jsb-value-types.name: only returns typeof, treating null and arrays as ordinary objects

jsb-number-validation.name: only uses parseFloat and mistakenly accepts values with units or infinite values.

files.script.js: function readAmount(text) { const amount = parseFloat(text); return Number.isNaN(amount) ? null : amount; }

jsb-math-round.name: rounds down, and the input close to the next gear also falls back to the previous gear.

jsb-string-normalize.name: is only converted to uppercase, retaining the white space at both ends.

jsb-string-slice.name: is intercepted from a fixed positive subscript, which is incorrect when the number of ticket numbers changes.

jsb-string-search.name: Only standardizes the search terms and forgets the title to be searched

files.script.js: function fillRoom(template, room) { return template.replace('{room}', () => room); }

jsb-strict-equality.name: Using ==, string numbers and numbers are treated as the same number

files.script.js: function sameSerial(left, right) { return left == right; }
function availableSeats(actual, planned) { return actual || planned; }

jsb-ternary.name: boundary usage >= causes the inventory to still be collected when it is zero

files.script.js: function stockLabel(count) { return count >= 0 ? 'can be collected' : 'To be replenished'; }

jsb-loop-flow.name: also writes "continue" when the package cannot be loaded, and mistakenly continues to load subsequent packages.

jsb-arrow-functions.name: uses block-level function body but forgets to return

jsb-rest-parameters.name: Ignore the first parameter and only calculate new batches

files.script.js: function shippedCount(prior, ...batches) { return batches.reduce((sum, next) => sum + next, 0); }

jsb-callback.name: The rules are written in the function and the received callback is not called.

jsb-closures.name: Add first and then return. The first number you received is too large.

jsb-recursion.name: Write the return value of the end condition as 1, totaling one more

files.script.js: function countBoxes(n) { if (n === 0) return 1; return n + countBoxes(n - 1); }
